captions.fig1_naming_turn: NAME titles (coined name before a colon or spaced dash) rose from 20.3% of ICLR submissions in 2023 to 40.5% in 2026 on a trend already running since 2017 (pre-trend OR 1.125/yr), and the camera-ready-free pool (rejected, withdrawn, desk-rejected; 40.3% in 2026) tracks all submissions. (a) The 2024 slope change is OR 1.098 [1.044, 1.154]/yr at paper level but 1.096 [0.990, 1.214] with year-level inference (NA pool 1.121 [1.019, 1.232]); only 2026 departs from the extrapolated 2017-23 trend (+5.5 pp [1.5, 9.5]). Aqua: name-masked abstract content counterfactuals (dotted line R1 fixed window; ribbon = range over R1/R3/R5 in the fixed and rolling designs), which explain 0.38-0.58 of the 2023-26 rise; the placebo window (trained 2018-20) already under-predicts 2021-23. (b) Annual change split into the part predicted by a rolling R1 content model and the unexplained part u; mean u rose by +1.35 pp (two-stage year-level 95% CI [0.03, 2.71]; year-label permutation p = 0.14).
captions.fig2_decomposition: Shares of the 2023-26 rise in NAME titles (Δ = 20.2 pp) attributed to abstract content, team composition and detectable LLM drafting; grey bands are the pre-registered predictions (content 0.20-0.50, composition ≤ 0.30, tool < 0.25). Name-masked content explains 0.38-0.49 in the fixed window and 0.56-0.58 in the rolling design, so 'content is a minority' is not established. Team size x new keys x LLM topic explains 0.26 of the 2023-26 rise by DFL reweighting (0.29 and 0.32 for 2024 and 2025, so the ≤ 0.30 prediction fails in 2025) but 0.09 net of content (Shapley). Detectable LLM drafting at A_max = 0.39 accounts for 7.1% [1.4, 12.9] after misclassification correction (3.1% by the pre-registered formula), but alternative fingerprints give up to 33%, so the tool share is small for the abstract fingerprint, not bounded in general; D3's slot positive control does not validate that fingerprint (slot OR 1.29 [0.92, 1.81]). The Shapley residual (unexplained by content or composition) is 0.57 [0.53, 0.62]. Content and composition CIs: conditional paper bootstrap (models fixed), B = 2000; tool-share CIs propagate the 95% CI of the fingerprint uplift δ.
captions.fig3_carriers: Who carries the NAME rise between E = 2022-23 and L = 2025-26 (declared profile keys; list position is a partition label only). (a) NAME change on papers grouped by how new their keys are, as a ratio of the population change (key-cluster bootstrap 95% CIs; right column: L-period papers). Papers whose keys are all stayer keys changed 0.06 [-0.14, 0.28] times the population change, papers whose keys all appeared in an earlier year 0.66 [0.49, 0.85], and last-position stayer keys on papers with an entrant first key 1.14 [1.07, 1.20]: the rise is graded by team newness. The pooled stayer-to-population ratios (ρ_last 0.995, ρ_any 0.816) are not identified as communal change, because a purely generational world with the observed co-authorship would give 0.78-0.93. (b) Generational increment G = 1 - slope of within-stayer on population change across 52 title style and 33 abstract topic markers: style markers move more slowly among stayer keys than topic markers (any position: G_style 0.17 [0.13, 0.20] vs G_topic -0.05 [-0.07, -0.03]), and the gap sits at the first list position (G_style 0.40). Holm p: H2a 0.005, H2b 0.005, H2d 0.005.
captions.fig4_register: LLM-favoured wording in titles (D3; associational). (a) Share of titles that fill a meaning-fixed opener slot with the LLM-favoured verb (Enhancing/Boosting vs Improving; Unveiling vs Understanding; Leveraging vs Exploiting; comprehensive vs systematic), pooled over slots, against control pairs (towards/toward, novel/new, via/using) in grey; bands are 95% Wilson intervals. The slot share moved from 0.34 in 2023 to 0.54 in 2024 (post OR 2.18 [1.41, 3.38] with slot-specific trends; controls 0.87 [0.64, 1.18]; slot-minus-control OR 2.55 [1.53, 4.25]); the 2023 cohort already deviates, so the shift is read as an acceleration from 2024, carried mainly by the improve slot. (b) Title rates per 1,000 of the R24 family, its neutral synonyms (N24) and the R26 family, all papers. From 2025 to 2026 R24 fell from 63.1 to 47.8 per 1,000 and R26 rose from 23.3 to 46.4; but the neutral synonyms fell alike (within-area RR 0.69 vs 0.74 for R24; R24 relative to N24 1.08 [0.86, 1.36]), so no register turnover is identified; R26 was chosen after the pilot saw it rise in these data. (c) Association of an abstract LLM fingerprint with the LLM-favoured slot variant (slot-filled papers) and with a NAME title on all papers of the same years, within topic100 × year (implied ORs from LPMs; joint topic100-cluster bootstrap, 95% CIs); right column: ratio OR_slot / OR_NAME. Pooled 2024-26: OR_slot 1.42 [1.14, 1.79] vs OR_NAME 1.14 [1.08, 1.21], ratio 1.24 [0.99, 1.57] (P(ratio ≤ 1) = 0.030); the pre-registered 1.5× is not met. 'D1 fingerprint' (F24 ≥ 2 words ∪ F26 ∪ typography) is the fingerprint behind D1's tool share; with it the slot association is OR 1.29 [0.92, 1.81], so the positive control does not validate that bound. The same-paper NAME comparator of the PLAN is not shown: it is conditioned on slot filling, a common effect of F and NAME. Holm p (pre-specified family): H3a <0.001, H3b 0.004 (not a valid test: R26 selected in-sample); H3d with the population comparator 0.030 (sensitivity family).
captions.fig5_stage_gains: Stage gains P(feature | passed stage) / P(feature | entered stage) for ICLR 2024-26 (year-standardised; paper bootstrap stratified by year, B = 2000, 95% CIs). (a) Desk screen, author exit (withdrawal before decision) and decision, and their product, the accepted/all ratio. NAME is slightly depleted before the decision (exit 0.974 [0.965, 0.983]) and enriched at it (decision 1.050 [1.028, 1.072]), netting to 1.021 (90% CI 1.001-1.041, inside the [0.90, 1.11] equivalence margin; editing-corrected on the complete arXiv audit: [0.949, 1.031]); with topic, area and team-size adjustment the stage gains are indistinguishable from 1 (exit 0.993, decision 1.019). The 2024 slope break does not differ detectably between accepted, rejected and withdrawn pools (ORs 1.05 / 1.12 / 1.11, equality p = 0.51; equivalence not shown). Outsider markers are under-represented among accepted papers (0.807 [0.749, 0.870]), almost entirely at the decision stage, where camera-ready recasing cannot be excluded; the LLM-style union total (0.975 [0.951, 1.001]) is not significant after Holm, and its pre-decision depletion is carried by R24 title words (without R24: 0.998 [0.972, 1.027]). Hollow markers: the decision stage, which is not identified against camera-ready edits (Figure 6b). (b) Accepted/all ratio by year (grey band: the pre-registered [0.95, 1.10] band for NAME). The LLM-style union was enriched among accepted papers in 2018-23 (1.154 [1.070, 1.236]) and is not after 2023; R24 words were depleted by the same amount before 2024.
captions.fig6_published_bias: How far a study of accepted papers alone would be from the full submission pool (2024-26). (a) Accepted-only / all-submission ratio for 24 pre-registered fashion statistics (95% CIs; dashed: random-selection null bands for entropy and JSD; hollow diamonds: OR statistics compared on the log-OR scale; grey band ±10%). Mainstream statistics are within ±10% in 9/11 cases (median |log ratio| 0.018); deviations concentrate in outsider (1/4 within) and LLM-style markers (7/9); the accepted-only Kobak-style LLM bound is 0.72 of the all-submission bound. A published-only study halves the 2024 NAME slope change (ratio of log-ORs 0.50 [-0.15, 1.16]). (b) Complete arXiv camera-ready audit (1311 pre-decision pairs, 2023-26; pre-decision v1 vs stored title; accepted minus rejected net flips, pseudo-flip 95% CI; F24: v1 vs stored abstract, 2024-26 pairs, tipping point for G_total). A decision-stage acceptance association is identified only if its tipping point D* lies beyond the CI and its identification p survives Holm across the 18 auditable title features (right column). For NAME the DiD is +1.48 pp [-0.63, 3.59] against D* = 2.92 pp; 0 of 26 title features pass (18 auditable); the NAME total ratio stays inside ±10% after the editing correction ([0.949, 1.031], 90%). F24 abstract DiD +0.71 pp [-1.95, 3.36]. ALL-CAPS titles, title typography and the abstract em dash cannot be audited through arXiv. Acceptance associations of title features are associational and not separated from camera-ready editing.
captions.table1_hypotheses: Pre-registered hypotheses H1a-H4e, the supporting tests S2.1-S2.2 and the decision-stage gate: prediction, regenerated estimate with 95% CI, final post-audit verdict and Holm-adjusted one-sided p within each direction.
captions.table2_acceleration: The NAME acceleration across pools, subsets, years and NAME definitions: segmented-logit slope change (primary 1.098 [1.044, 1.154]), its year-level analogue, the LPM slope change, and the acceleration of content-unexplained drift Δu.
captions.table3_content_bracket: Content-counterfactual bracket: share of the NAME rise predicted by each abstract representation (name-masked R1/R3/R5, coarse and leaky brackets) in the fixed, rolling and placebo designs, with out-of-sample AUC and the implied acceleration of unexplained drift.
captions.table4_filter_audit: Stage-wise filter gains (desk, exit, decision, total) for mainstream, outsider and LLM-style features in 2024-26, with the camera-ready audit's net-flip DiD and tipping point for each auditable feature.
